author: Gaetan Ferry
title: GitHub App Private Keys: 474 Leaked Keys Exposed
attributed_claim_summary: GitGuardian's own September 2026 investigation selected 4,802 GitHub-context private-key candidates from more than 500,000 previously detected RSA keys and reported that 474 keys authenticated as 440 GitHub Apps. Reported access included high-privilege apps; these results have not been independently reproduced.
evidence_or_event: First-party research article published on September 22, 2026 by Gaetan Ferry, describing vendor-performed API validation and permissions analysis of a selected set of previously leaked GitHub App private keys. Underlying leak examples included 2020–2025 and are not new 2026 leak incidents.
limitations: Selection-conditioned result: 474/4,802 is NOT an ecosystem-wide GitHub App key leakage rate; no random frame, externally authenticated key-pool provenance, independent replication, sensitivity/specificity denominator, or evidence of GitGuardian preventing incidents. Original article content was accessed via public indexed publisher content, and direct-page retrieval intermittently failed. No raw keys, screenshots, personal records or exploit instructions retained. Do not treat syndicated retellings as independent confirmation.
research_relevance: Machine identity governance: a forgotten non-expiring GitHub App private key with broad scopes can create a downstream supply-chain exposure path. Security and code reuse require least privilege, inventory, safe key rotation and independently tested fail-closed workflows.
practical_experiment: Freeze nonworking synthetic GitHub App-key-form fixture cases and independent hidden acceptance tests; compare existing GitHub App scope/inventory and CI security controls to a bounded, version-pinned ggshield integration in an isolated disposable repository. Measure missed/false alerts, unauthorized context/network exposure, accepted-task outcomes and reviewer minutes; do not test actual keys or claim population prevalence.
